name: MAX6035BAUR50+T
title: MAX6035: precision series voltage reference to 33 V supply, 2.5 V, 3.0 V and 5.0 V, in SOT23 and SO
summary: A three-terminal series-mode reference that runs from supplies up to 33 V while drawing a nearly constant 73 µA typical. Fixed outputs of 2.5 V, 3.0 V and 5.0 V come in an A grade (±0.2%, 25 ppm/°C max from -40 °C to +85 °C) and a B grade (±0.5%, 65 ppm/°C max) in a 3-pin SOT23, plus a 2.5 V version in an 8-pin SO. It sources 10 mA, sinks 2 mA, needs no output capacitor and stays stable with up to 5 µF on the output. MAX6035BAUR50+T is the 5.0 V B-grade SOT23 part on tape and reel.
key_figures: up to 33 V (6.9 V min for 5.0 V)

circuits.title: Typical operating circuit
circuits.description: The reference in its basic use: the supply goes straight to IN, GND to ground, and OUT is the reference voltage. A 0.1 µF capacitor from IN to ground is optional; it helps with fast line changes. No output capacitor is needed.

circuits.title: Load-transient test circuit (Figure 1)
circuits.description: Measures the response to a step in load current in both directions. A square-wave source VL switching between 0 V and twice VOUT drives the output through RL, so the reference alternately sources and sinks VOUT/RL. CL sets the output load capacitance.

parts.note: 0 or 1 µF in the load-transient graphs

circuits.title: Load-transient test circuit (Figure 2)
circuits.description: Measures the response to a step in sourced load current. The square-wave source VL switches between 0 V and VOUT behind RL, so the load current steps between VOUT/RL and zero.

parts.note: 0 or 1 µF in the load-transient graphs

where.ΔVOUT(max): widest spread of output voltage over the temperature range, in ppm of VOUT

operation.text: Being a series reference, the device needs no external resistor and draws load current from the input only while the load takes it. Its own supply current is 73 µA typical and moves by no more than 0.7 µA per volt of input. A shunt reference, by contrast, sits behind a series resistor, so its current changes with input voltage and must be set for the largest load even when the load is absent.
A 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor from IN to ground, placed as near the device as possible, gives the best line-transient response. Where transient response matters little, it can be left off.

The output is stable with no capacitor at all and with loads up to 5 µF. Where the load or supply steps, an output capacitor of 0.1 µF or more lowers overshoot and undershoot and improves the transient response.
Output settles to within 0.1% of its final value in about 240 µs typical; more output capacitance lengthens this.
After a cycle across the full operating temperature range, the output at +25 °C shifts by 135 ppm typical from its value before the cycle.

OUT may be shorted to GND or IN indefinitely, within the continuous power-dissipation rating; the short-circuit current is 27 mA typical to GND and -4 mA typical to IN. At the full 10 mA source current the package dissipation limit must still be observed.

For a data converter whose reference-induced error must stay below 1 LSB across its operating temperature span, the largest allowable reference temperature coefficient falls as that span widens and as resolution rises from 8 to 20 bits, with reference drift taken as the only error. Total converter accuracy also depends on integral and differential nonlinearity, offset error and gain error.

It fits as an upgrade for REF02 and REF43 class references, at 14 times less power than the REF02 and 5 times less than the REF43, moving from an 8-pin SO to a 3-pin SOT23. A curvature-correction circuit and laser-trimmed thin-film resistors give the low temperature coefficient.
Uses named for it: 4 mA to 20 mA industrial control loops, Li+ battery chargers, 12-bit A/D and D/A converters, digital multimeters, portable data-acquisition systems and low-power test equipment.
